title: Inequalities: Number Lines, Integer Solutions and Solving
seo_title: Year 8 Inequalities Worksheets: Number Lines, Listing Integers and Solving Linear Inequalities
standard_text: Use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥; use algebraic methods to solve linear equations in one variable; solve linear inequalities in one variable and represent the solution set on a number line.

key_big: Solve an inequality like an equation. If you divide by a negative, reverse the sign.
key_sub: On a number line, an open circle means not included (< or >), a filled circle means included (≤ or ≥).
body_html:
How it works

< less than, > greater than, ≤ less than or equal to, ≥ greater than or equal to. On a number line an open circle means the number is not included and a filled circle means it is.

Solve an inequality like an equation, but if you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the sign.

Example

Solve 3x + 4 < 19.

Subtract 4: 3x < 15.

Divide by 3.

Answer: x < 5

Example

Solve 7 − 2x ≥ 1.

Subtract 7: −2x ≥ −6.

Divide by −2 and reverse the sign.

Answer: x ≤ 3

Example

List the integers with −2 < n ≤ 3.

−2 is not included; 3 is.

Answer: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up open and filled circles.
  • Including an end that is not allowed: −2 < n does not include −2.
  • Forgetting to reverse the sign when dividing by a negative number.
  • Writing = instead of an inequality sign in the answer.

faq.q: What is the difference between < and ≤?
faq.a: x < 5 means x is less than 5, so 5 is not included. x ≤ 5 includes 5.

faq.q: Why do I reverse the sign when dividing by a negative?
faq.a: Multiplying by a negative flips the order of numbers: 2 < 3 but −2 > −3. So the inequality sign must flip too.

faq.q: How do I show an inequality on a number line?
faq.a: Draw a circle at the number, filled if it is included and open if not, and a line or arrow over all the values that work.
At least means greater than or equal to (≥). “At most” means less than or equal to (≤).

items.q: A lift can carry at most 8 people. Which inequality shows the number of people p?
items.e: “At most 8” means 8 or fewer: p ≤ 8.

items.q: You must be over 12 to watch a film. Which inequality shows the age a?
items.e: “Over 12” does not include 12: a > 12.

items.q: Ava has £20. Tickets cost £3 each. What is the greatest number of tickets she can buy?
items.e: 3t ≤ 20, so t ≤ 6.67. She can buy 6 tickets.

items.q: A taxi costs £4 plus £2 per mile. Leo has £15. What is the greatest whole number of miles he can travel?
items.e: 4 + 2m ≤ 15, so m ≤ 5.5. The greatest whole number is 5.
